title: The agent-ready web: Simplify user actions with WebMCP — Tara Agyemang, Google
talk_summary: Tara Agyemang presents WebMCP, a proposed Chrome standard for exposing website capabilities as structured tools to in-browser AI agents instead of relying on DOM/screenshot scraping. She demos declarative form attributes and imperative registerTool APIs, plus inspector/eval tooling, while stressing it is an early experimental preview.

takeaways.what_they_do: Define site/app capabilities as JSON-schema tools with descriptions and execute handlers that return results, so agents call explicit actions instead of parsing DOM, accessibility trees, and screenshots.
takeaways.evidence_quote: instead of any agent guessing what your website does, you're kind of giving the AI agent a menu of tools

takeaways.technique: Descriptive tool schemas and return payloads
takeaways.what_they_do: Manually create tool name/description/schema and make descriptions explicit enough for the agent to know when to call the tool; execute returns information for the next step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you want to make sure you have really descriptive descriptions that enable the AI agent to know when it should be calling this tool

takeaways.what_they_do: A Chrome extension lists tools found on a page and lets users prompt or call tools directly; an eval CLI helps test WebMCP tools on sites.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's an eval CLI tool you can use to help you start testing your own sites in the Web MCP tools

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the user in the loop for real-money checkout and keep UI state synced with tool calls so the human can see and approve what the agent did.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You'll probably want your user to manually do that step so they know that they're spending real money.

takeaways.what_they_do: Improve semantic HTML, accessibility, page performance, and UX flows first; accessible sites are also easier for agents to understand.
takeaways.evidence_quote: making your site accessible for everyone makes it accessible to AI agents by default

takeaways.what_they_do: Only expose tools relevant to the current page/state; the start page has one tool, while the maze page exposes navigation and item tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: on this page, we have a bunch of new tools in the scope of this page, whereas the previous page only had that one tool
